transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-20
Start time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~1:35
Location: All-hands Zoom (recorded)
Recording link: https://redwood.zoom/rec/aug2026-ah
Deck: drive/redwood/allhands/2026-08-august-alignment.pdf

Attendees (salient): Maya Chen (CEO); Liam O'Connor (CTO); Priya Patel (Head of Product); Diego Ramos (VP Eng); Sara Lin (Head of People); Omar Farouk (Research lead); plus ~120 attendees across eng/product/sales/support.

SUMMARY:
- Big focus: Q4 ops & capacity planning, Optimize beta rollout, hiring priorities, and company gratitude / recognition segment.
- Leadership updates on runway, revenue growth, and customer traction; short note on competitive landscape.
- Clear next steps assigned for capacity plan, product rollout checklist, and hiring communications.

TOPICS COVERED:
1) Business health & roadmap cadence
2) Redwood Optimize beta and effects on unit economics
3) Dedicated/Private customer wins and compliance asks
4) Hiring and resource prioritization
5) Shoutouts / gratitude and culture items

ACTION ITEM SUMMARY (auto): see action_items metadata.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect) ---
00:00 Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, it is 5pm UTC. Welcome to the August alignment and gratitude huddle. Um quick ask, if you're on mute please unmute if you want to clap during shoutouts—jk. We have about an hour and a half.
00:20 Maya: Quick safety note, recording is on, deck is in the drive. We'll run through high-level ops and then leave time for q's. Liam, quick state of the world?
00:32 Liam: Thanks Maya. Quick bullets — revenue's tracking slightly above plan, enterprise net-new deals are healthy, we closed two Dedicated contracts last month and a Private deployment pilot started with a regulated customer in EMEA. Latency SLOs are holding, cost per token improved after a set of kernel tweaks shipping last sprint. A lot of credit to infra and research.
00:56 Speaker 1 (maybe Diego): There's also a note on capacity — we've seen a 22% spike in long-tail async workloads, queuing peeks in two regions if we don't reserve more burst.
01:10 Maya: Ok good, that's why we need the Q4 plan. Diego?
01:16 Diego: Yeah, so engineering's working on two tracks — short-term burst capacity for autumn (reserve extra Dedicated nodes), and a mid-term runtime workstream: batching improvements + prefix cache improvements. We have a draft plan in the wiki, link in the deck. We'll publish a finalized plan by next Friday.
01:34 (crosstalk)
01:36 Priya: On product, Optimize beta went into a small closed group last week. First signals: suggested batching configs reduced per-token cost by 8-12% on average for text-gen workloads, and the model recommendation engine flagged a few quantized variants that gave 4-6% latency wins. This is early.
02:02 Omar: To add — research ran microbenchmarks on MPT-family and Llama-3 variants; kernel-level changes gave 10% speedups on longer sequences but there are some edge cases with KV cache eviction that we need to test. Some transcribed notes came back as K-V cash in the logs ha.
02:24 Liam: We're prioritizing two kernel optimizations for MPT where it moves the needle most.
02:30 Maya: Thanks. Quick note on customers — we've had more compliance asks, SOC2 plus ISO coming more frequently; our Private packaging is helping land more regulated customers. Sara, anything to add re: hiring?
02:46 Sara: Yes — hiring velocity is slightly down month-over-month. We have open reqs prioritized: 1) infra/GPU runtime, 2) core infra SRE, 3) product analytics, 4) senior SEs for Solutions. We're adjusting referral incentive for critical hires and will send the updated priorities out tomorrow.
03:06 Tom H. (Sales): On renewals — customers are asking for clearer cost breakdowns per route; Console improvements here will be high impact.
03:20 Priya: Agreed, Console will get a per-route cost breakdown so AE can share with customers. That will be in the next sprint.
03:30 Audience Q (typed): Will Optimize change existing APIs?
03:36 Priya: Short answer: no breaking changes. Optimize will recommend batching/caching/quant settings and can be toggled per-customer. We'll provide a migration guide.
03:46 Audience Q: Any update on pricing model for hosted vs dedicated?
03:52 Maya: We're evaluating options, goal is to make units predictable for customers while keeping margin. Finance will run elasticity modeling and we'll share a proposal next month.
04:05 Liam: One thing I want to call out — there are tradeoffs between latency SLOs and cost when caching is more aggressive. For some customers we will surface a simple slider: latency-priority vs cost-priority.
04:26 Diego: On the capacity plan itself — we need input from product and sales on committed vs expected traffic. Diego: please poke your PMs for forecasts.
04:40 (brief pause while attendees scroll deck)
04:48 Maya: Quick shoutouts — we have a long list of kudos in the doc. I'll call out a few: E2E infra reliability from K. Singh and team after the kernel rollback handling; Solutions team for the POC that turned into a Dedicated contract; People Ops for the onboarding revamp.
05:12 (applause emoji in chat)
05:20 Sara: Also happy birthday shout to R. Kim in People Ops — not to derail but celebration matters.
05:30 Maya: Now a short transparency moment on runway and hiring. We have runway into mid-2027 given current projections, assuming we hit plan. We are actively fundraising — small raise to extend runway and accelerate Private offering. This is sensitive; we'll share a short comms doc tomorrow.
06:00 Audience whisper / Speaker 2: Is this a down round?
06:04 Maya: Not at all. It's a targeted round. We will publish FAQs for managers.
06:12 (some folks typing in chat)
06:20 Priya: Back to product — timeline: Optimize beta to broader customer cohort in Sept, Console cost breakdown into next sprint, and rollout of model suggestions and quant profiles will be staged. We'll have a public beta sign-up.
06:42 Omar: Research note — the kernel optimizations are nontrivial; QA needs more time on LLM workloads that have long histories. We're adding an automated regression suite focused on generation fidelity.
07:02 Liam: Also want to flag infrastructure cost: some of our older clusters are expensive; we're evaluating a controlled migration to more cost-efficient instance families. This will reduce monthly spend if we can maintain perf.
07:22 Audience Q: Competitors question — are we worried about commoditization from major cloud providers?
07:28 Maya: We are aware; our bet is that teams choose a provider that balances cost, performance, and operational tooling. Our differentiation is the developer experience and predictable economics. We track Anthropic and OpenAI product moves closely.
07:46 Diego: We also watch hardware vendors — NVIDIA's new releases change cost calculus for customers — but they also open possibilities for lower-latency kernels.
08:02 (minute marker, moving on)
08:05 Culture & recognition block — 10 min of shoutouts, nominations came from team leads.
08:12 Speaker 3 (engineering lead): Big shout to the infra on-call who handled a flapping region incident, and to the research pair that squashed a degenerate generation bug in the reranker.
08:30 (intermittent applause in chat)
08:36 People ops short update: We're launching an internal mentoring program, signups open next week. Also, updated parental leave policy goes into effect Sept 1.
08:55 Maya: OK quick wrap — the three priority asks for the next two weeks: 1) finalize Q4 capacity plan (Diego), 2) share Optimize rollout checklist and invites (Priya), 3) updated hiring priorities and referral note (Sara).
09:15 Q&A open floor (rapidfire):
09:20 Attendee: Will Private deployments support HSM integrations?
09:24 Liam: Yes — HSM/KMS integration is in scope for Private, we have partners in process. Some implementation work remains but it's prioritized.
09:38 Attendee: How will we communicate fundraising to customers?
09:42 Maya: We'll give a short, transparent note focused on continued product stability and roadmap; won't disclose terms until closed. Managers will get an FAQ.
09:55 (short technical sidebar)
10:10 Diego: On the capacity numbers — if we assume 15% month-over-month growth in async workloads we need to reserve an extra 120 GPU-hours/week for Q4. Details in the draft plan.
10:30 Priya: Also a reminder — customer feedback loop: send product signals to the #product-io channel with context so we can triage.
10:40 Final pulses: managers to run team retros on hiring slippage and surface blockers.
10:50 Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a short pulse email and action items. Appreciate all the work. Shoutouts again — big thanks to infra, research, and people ops this month.
11:05 (meeting ends; recording stops)
